attempts.summary: On node1, cron scheduling is now restricted to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow (with /etc/cron.deny removed so cron.allow is authoritative). Created the opsadmin user, verified root and opsadmin can install/list crontabs while a test unprivileged user is rejected by crontab with "not allowed to use this program". Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id (83a0a80f...), issued a non-blocking systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed a new boot_id (df4b7e15...) and fresh uptime, then re-verified crond is active and the cron.allow restriction (root/opsadmin allowed, unlisted user denied) still holds post-restart.
